chunks: And ʿAmr ibn Shimr narrated from Jābir, who said:
I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the midwife: is it permissible for the newborn child to marry her?
He عليه السلام said: "No, nor her daughter. She is like one of his mothers."

key_terms.أُمَّهَاتِهِ: his mothers, indicating a maternal-like prohibited status
key_terms.الْقَابِلَةِ: the midwife who assists in childbirth
key_terms.لِلْمَوْلُودِ: for the child who was delivered

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia fiqh for a person to marry the midwife who delivered him or her daughter?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning marriage relations established through the role of a midwife. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that the person delivered by the midwife may not marry her, nor her daughter, because she holds a status comparable to one of his mothers.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4431 - Amr ibn Shimr reported from Jabir, who said:
I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), about the midwife, whether it is permissible for the child she delivered to marry her.
Imam (as) replied: "No, nor her daughter. She is like one of his mothers."
